commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Clarify dictionary state when lz_init() fails

lzma_lz_decoder_init() may be reinitializing a coder that was used
successfully earlier. Spell out the lz_init() error path explicitly
instead of hiding it behind return_if_error(): lz_init() never touches
coder->dict, so if it fails, the existing dictionary buffer (if any)
from an earlier successful initialization is untouched and remains
valid for the next initialization attempt.

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the filter chain should be cleaned up with
lzma_next_end() so that a later reinitialization attempt starts from a
clean state. lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init() have
always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.

The following decoders initialize the LZMA1 filter directly without
using the raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all
other filters when a program is linked against static liblzma. These
functions didn't call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error:

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

Make them call lzma_next_end() when lzma_next_filter_init() fails,
except when it fails with LZMA_MEM_ERROR: in that case no new coder
could have been attached to the chain, so there's nothing to clean up.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)

coupling: Both commits independently remove one of two redundant defenses against a stale lzma_lz_decoder coder state after a failed dictionary reallocation on reinit of lzma_alone_decoder()/lzma_lzip_decoder()/lzma_microlzma_decoder(). (1) e316ad6 (edited) drops the `coder->dict.size = 0;` reset that upstream performs before freeing/reallocating coder->dict.buf, so after a failed realloc, dict.size is left stale (matching an earlier, now-freed allocation) while dict.buf is NULL. (2) 4e4fc77 (edited) adds a carve-out that skips the lzma_next_end() teardown of the inner LZMA1/LZ coder specifically when lzma_next_filter_init() fails with LZMA_MEM_ERROR, so the stale {dict.buf=NULL, dict.size=stale} state is never destroyed and recreated from scratch. Either fix alone is sufficient to prevent the bug: if e316ad6 is correct, dict.size becomes 0 on failure, which forces a fresh reallocation on the next reinit regardless of whether teardown happened; if 4e4fc77 is correct, the entire inner coder (including the stale dict.size) is freed and NULLed on any failure, so the next reinit always starts fresh. Only when BOTH are weakened does a reinit with a dictionary size that coincidentally matches the earlier (pre-failure) size skip reallocation entirely and dereference the NULL/freed dict.buf. A fix touching only one of the two commits' diffs leaves the other redundant path intact and the bug unreachable; both must be repaired together.
